text.p: Mercury Finance Co, a consumer finance and insurance company, said it restated its 1995 results because of the way it accounted for certain single-interest insurance transactions.

The restatement, which increased the allowance for loan losses by $17 million, reduced previously reported net income by $12 million or $0.07 per share. Restated 1995 net income was $98.9 million, or $0.57.
For the third quarter of 1996, Mercury posted earnings of $15.9 million, or $0.09 per share, compared with year-earlier earnings of $28.5 million, or $0.16 per share.
The most recent quarter includes an after-tax charge of $20.5 million reflecting the adoption of a static pooling method of acounting for reserves.
Before the adjustment to loss reserves based on the new method of calculating future losses, Mercury had net income of $36.4 million, or $0.21 per share.
In the past, Mercury analyzed the adequacy of its reserves on a total portfolio basis. It said static pooling enables for a more comprehensive analysis.
